---
name: political-text-opt-out
description: >-
  Use when someone wants their US phone number off political campaign, PAC,
  party, or advocacy group text and call lists, or reports unwanted political
  texts or calls.
---
# Political Text & Call Opt-Out Playbook

## Set expectations (tell the user plainly)
- Political calls and texts are exempt from the National Do Not Call Registry.
- Autodialed/mass political texts and prerecorded calls to cells need prior consent; peer-to-peer (P2P) texts sent one at a time by a person do not. The goal is a big reduction, not zero.
- STOP works one organization at a time: texting platforms keep opt-out lists per client.
- A reply of stop, quit, end, revoke, opt out, cancel, or unsubscribe must be honored within 10 business days (47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10), as revised by FCC 26-67, effective Nov 25, 2026). Senders may send one confirmation and may treat the opt-out as covering only that category of informational message.
- Numbers come from donating or signing petitions (committees share/trade lists), voter files with a phone number, and commercial data vendors matching phones to voter records.
- Timing: STOP within days; data vendors 1 to 6 weeks (Data Trust 15 business days; Aristotle 45 to 90 days). Recheck monthly and before primaries and general elections.

## Step 1: Collect
1. Each phone number to protect; confirm it is the user's or they are authorized for it.
2. Full legal name, current address and recent past addresses, an email for confirmations, and state.
3. Optional screenshots of recent political texts. Record sending number/short code, the "Paid for by" organization, and any link domain.
4. Never ask for ID up front; only if a vendor requires it. Never create or alter documents.

## Step 2: Per-sender actions (user does these on their phone; you guide)
1. Reply exactly `STOP` to each political text as its own message. For P2P texts they can add "Please remove my number from all your lists." Never reply to texts that look like scams; report them instead.
2. Forward unwanted texts to 7726 (SPAM) and tap Report Junk / Report spam.
3. Texts continuing 10+ business days after STOP, or autodialed without consent: FCC complaint at https://consumercomplaints.fcc.gov/hc/en-us (1-888-225-5322) with date, sending number, org, and STOP date. State AG: https://www.naag.org/find-my-ag/. Scam-looking texts: https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/
4. Filters: iPhone https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/screen-and-filter-texts-iph203ab0be4/ios ; Google Messages https://support.google.com/messages/answer/9061432 ; Verizon Call Filter https://www.verizon.com/solutions-and-services/add-ons/protection-and-security/call-filter/ ; T-Mobile Scam Shield https://www.t-mobile.com/benefits/scam-shield ; AT&T ActiveArmor https://www.att.com/security/active-armor/ . Carrier filters mainly catch spam and may miss legitimate political texts.

## Step 3: Upstream opt-outs
Rules: do web forms in your browser, pausing for the user at certifications, email checks, captchas you can't pass, or ID uploads. Draft every email and show it to the user; send only after their explicit approval, from their own email. One request per number, with name and address.

### Voter-file and data vendors (highest impact)
- L2: web form https://l2-data.com/optout1-667457/ or email privacy@L2Political.com. CA residents: https://l2-data.com/california-privacy-rights-for-california-residents-only/
- TargetSmart: https://privacy.targetsmart.com/do-not-sell-my-personal-information or 1-888-678-6880. Email requests not accepted. May verify by mail.
- Catalist: https://catalist.us/your-privacy-choices/ or (800) 938-9516. Choose delete and opt out of sale. Honored from any state.
- i360: https://www.i-360.com/disclosures/ (links to its request form); CA https://www.i-360.com/ccpa/ or 1-844-611-2737.
- Data Trust: https://thedatatrust.com/your-privacy-choices/ or (855) 695-5575; privacy@thedatatrust.com.
- Aristotle (CA residents only): https://www.aristotle.com/ccpa-faqs/ or 888-217-9600. Says voter-file data can't be deleted.
- California DROP (CA only, free, reaches 600+ brokers): https://privacy.ca.gov/drop/
- Decision Desk HQ (low priority, says it doesn't sell): privacy@decisiondeskhq.com; requires ID plus utility bill.

### Party committees
- DNC: https://ak.democrats.org/signup/text-message-preferences/ ; info@democrats.org
- RNC: email email@gop.com with subject "Unsubscribe", or text STOP to 80810 / 94646; help contactus.rnc@gop.com
- DCCC: info@dccc.org (opt out of sale/list exchange and texts)
- DSCC: privacy@dscc.org
- NRCC: info@nrccvictory.com
- NRSC: Privacy@NRSC.org; short code 55404 (reply STOP)

### Donation platforms
- ActBlue doesn't text; delete the phone from the ActBlue Express profile: https://help.actblue.com/hc/en-us/articles/16869091765143-how-do-i-delete-my-phone-number-from-my-account . Reply STOP to each group.
- WinRed doesn't text: https://support.winred.com/en/articles/3218288-how-do-i-unsubscribe-from-texts-or-emails ; sender lookup https://support.winred.com/en/articles/9205169-who-is-emailing-or-texting-me

### Texting platforms (mostly route you back to the sender)
- Opn Sesame: if added without permission, email info@opnsesame.com with your number and the sending number.
- Tatango: cs@tatango.com
- Scale to Win, ThruText/GetThru, Hustle, CallHub, RumbleUp: opt-out is per organization; reply STOP as a standalone message. Never reply START to Hustle texts (it re-subscribes).

### Email template (draft for approval)
Subject: Request to delete my personal information and opt out of sale or sharing – [Full Name]

> I request that you delete my personal information, stop selling or sharing it, and add my phone number(s) to your suppression and do-not-contact list.
> Name: [Full legal name]
> Address: [Current address] (previous: [prior, if any])
> Phone(s): [numbers]
> Email: [email]
> Please confirm in writing when this is complete. If you need to verify my identity, tell me exactly what you need.
> [Name]

## Step 4: Voter registration record
The phone field on the federal voter registration form is optional. States differ on releasing voter phones. Find the state election office at https://www.eac.gov/voters/register-and-vote-in-your-state or https://www.nass.org/can-I-vote and ask whether it releases phone numbers and how to remove one (often by updating registration with the phone left blank). Never cancel or change anything else; warn the user not to unregister by accident.

## Step 5: Track everything
Keep a table on your computer and update it on every change:
`date | target | number(s) | method | status (sent/pending user/confirmed/rejected) | follow-up date | notes`
Follow-ups: 10 business days after STOP, 45 days for vendors, 90 days for Aristotle and DROP.

## Step 6: Report back
Tell the user what's done, what's waiting on them (emails to approve, ID requests, email checks), and what's pending with expected dates. Offer a monthly recheck routine that follows up on pending requests, handles new senders, and drafts FCC complaints for texts that keep coming.

skills.name: political-text-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of a political-text opt-out bot, to collect what's needed before running political-text-opt-out.
skills.content:
---
name: political-text-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of a political-text opt-out
  bot, to collect what's needed before running political-text-opt-out.
---
Open with one line: you're here to get their phone number off political campaign, PAC, party, and advocacy group text and call lists, at the source as well as sender by sender.

Then ask one question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which phone number or numbers should come off the lists? Confirm they're theirs.
2. Their full name and state, plus current address and any recent past ones (data vendors match on these). Save the address to their vault, not memory.
3. Optional: screenshots of a few recent political texts, to identify senders and platforms.
4. Whether to connect their Gmail or Outlook so you can draft removal emails for their approval and watch for confirmations. Nothing is sent without their OK; if they decline, give them drafts to copy and send.

Give one honest note: political texts are exempt from the Do Not Call Registry and volunteer-sent texts don't need consent, so this cuts volume a lot but may not reach zero.

Save the number(s), name, and state to memory, then run political-text-opt-out.

Finally, offer a monthly recheck routine that follows up on pending requests, handles new senders, and ramps up before elections; create it if they say yes.
